title: The Firebird, Suite (1919)
hook: A magic bird, a captive princess and an immortal sorcerer in the Russian fairy tale that made Stravinsky famous overnight.

painting.title: Ivan Tsarevich on the Grey Wolf
painting.pairingNote: Prince Ivan, the hero of the ballet, escapes through a dark forest with his princess on the back of the magic grey wolf, a scene from the same Russian fairy tale of the Firebird that Stravinsky’s collaborators drew on.

facts: *The Firebird* was Stravinsky’s first ballet, written in 1909–10 for Sergei Diaghilev’s Ballets Russes. Diaghilev wanted a ballet on a Russian subject for the 1910 Paris season. He first asked other composers, then gave the commission to Stravinsky, who was 27 and almost unknown.

The premiere at the Paris Opéra on 25 June 1910, with choreography by Michel Fokine and Tamara Karsavina as the Firebird, was an immediate success and made Stravinsky famous overnight. Three years later he would shock the same city with *The Rite of Spring*.

The story comes from Russian fairy tales. Prince Ivan strays into the magic garden of the immortal sorcerer Kashchei, catches the Firebird and lets her go in return for one of her feathers. He falls in love with a captive princess. When Kashchei’s monsters seize him, he waves the feather; the Firebird makes them dance until they drop, sings them to sleep, and shows Ivan the egg that holds Kashchei’s soul. Ivan breaks it, the spell is lifted, and everyone celebrates.

The full ballet needs a huge orchestra and lasts about 45 minutes. In 1919, living in Switzerland, Stravinsky made a shorter concert suite for a smaller orchestra. It is the version heard most often today.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a dark enchanted garden (I), the Firebird’s flight (II), the princesses’ round dance (III), the monsters’ frenzy (IV), a lullaby (V) and a sunrise of celebration (VI).

movements.heading: Introduction
movements.title: Introduction
movements.summary: Night in Kashchei’s enchanted garden, where his enemies stand turned to stone. Low strings mutter a slow, dark phrase; above them the violins slide in eerie, glassy sounds. Strange colours flicker in the woodwinds. It is music of mystery rather than melody, and it begins so quietly that it is almost not there.

mainIdeas.name: The magic phrase
mainIdeas.description: a few slow notes creeping up and down in the cellos and basses, the musical sign of the supernatural.

mainIdeas.name: Glassy string slides
mainIdeas.description: violins playing [[harmonics|harmonics]] while sliding along the string, one of the effects with which Stravinsky said he tried to outdo his teacher Rimsky-Korsakov.

stops.hear: Very softly, the cellos and basses mutter a slow, dark phrase
High, ghostly, sliding sounds in the violins
Flickers in the woodwinds and a muted horn; the dark phrase returns
Quick flashes of colour rising through the orchestra

notice: Listen to the opening. Richard Strauss told Stravinsky he should have begun with a crash to astonish the audience; Stravinsky chose almost silence instead.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Robert Shaw, best known as a choral conductor, was music director of the Atlanta Symphony Orchestra when he made this recording in June 1978. It was one of the first orchestral recordings made digitally, for the Cleveland label Telarc. On the Spotify album the suite is tracks 1–6.

movements.heading: The Firebird and its Dance – Variation of the Firebird
movements.title: The Firebird and its Dance – Variation of the Firebird
movements.summary: The Firebird darts into the garden, a creature of light and speed. Brilliant, fluttering figures shoot through the woodwinds and strings, never settling. This is a dance without a tune: all wings, flashes and glitter.

mainIdeas.name: The Firebird’s flight
mainIdeas.description: fast, fluttering figures in flutes, clarinets and violins, with sudden accents and trills.

stops.hear: Rapid, glittering flurries in the woodwinds and strings
Fast, flickering figures leaping from instrument to instrument
The flurries grow more brilliant, with sharp accents

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: A last shimmer, and the music vanishes

notice: Try to follow a single line here. It is almost impossible: Stravinsky makes the orchestra sound like feathers catching the light.

movements.heading: The Princesses' Khorovod
movements.title: The Princesses' Khorovod
movements.summary: Thirteen princesses held captive by Kashchei come out into the garden and dance a khorovod, a slow Russian round dance. Prince Ivan has fallen in love with one of them. The melody, gentle and a little melancholy, is a Russian folk song that Rimsky-Korsakov, Stravinsky’s teacher, had also used.

mainIdeas.name: The round-dance melody
mainIdeas.description: a calm, folk-like tune, first on the oboe, later in the strings.

stops.hear: Flutes and a harp play softly, then an oboe begins a gentle, folk-like tune
Other woodwinds answer the oboe; the tune is passed around
The cellos and then the violins take the melody, warmer and fuller
stops.happening: Ivan watches the princess he loves

stops.hear: The tune returns softly in the woodwinds
stops.happening: The dance draws to a close

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: Very quiet, sustained chords
stops.happening: Dawn is near; the princesses must return

notice: This is the only movement built on a real tune you could sing. Notice how calm it is next to the magic music around it.

movements.heading: Infernal Dance of King Kashchei
movements.title: Infernal Dance of King Kashchei
movements.summary: Kashchei’s monsters have seized Ivan. He waves the Firebird’s feather, and the Firebird casts a spell: the whole court must dance, faster and faster, until they collapse. After a sudden, violent crash, the music hammers out jagged, off-beat rhythms; a long, swaying melody in the strings sweeps through the middle; brass slide and roar towards the end.

mainIdeas.name: The jagged dance
mainIdeas.description: short, stabbing phrases in the low brass and bassoons, with accents in the wrong places.

mainIdeas.name: The swaying melody
mainIdeas.description: a broad, lyrical line in the strings, carried along by the frantic rhythm.

stops.hear: A huge, sudden crash, then low instruments stab out a jagged rhythm
stops.happening: The spell: the monsters must dance

stops.hear: Fast, off-beat accents and a xylophone flash
The strings sing a long, swaying melody over the pounding rhythm
stops.happening: The second theme of the dance

stops.hear: The rhythms grow wilder; brass and percussion pile on
Roaring brass slides and the loudest music of the suite

stops.label: Last 15 seconds
stops.hear: Crashing chords, then the music collapses

notice: Listen to the accents. They keep landing off the beat, so the dance seems to stumble forward, never comfortable.

movements.heading: Berceuse
movements.title: Berceuse
movements.summary: The Firebird sings the exhausted monsters to sleep. Over a gently rocking harp and muted strings, a bassoon plays a long, sad, lulling melody. Then the music sinks into a hushed shimmer of strings that leads, without a break, into the finale.

mainIdeas.name: The lullaby
mainIdeas.description: a slow, drooping melody on the bassoon, later taken up by the oboe and strings.

mainIdeas.name: The rocking accompaniment
mainIdeas.description: harp and violas swaying back and forth.

stops.hear: A harp rocks gently; a bassoon plays a slow, sad melody
An oboe takes the melody, high and tender
The strings join with the tune, warmer and fuller
The bassoon returns with the opening melody

stops.label: Last 40 seconds
stops.hear: A very quiet, trembling shimmer in the strings, almost still
stops.happening: Darkness; the music runs straight on into the finale

notice: The bassoon usually plays low, comic or gruff parts. Here Stravinsky gives it a lullaby, and the effect is strange and beautiful.

movements.heading: Finale
movements.title: Finale
movements.summary: Ivan has broken the egg; Kashchei is dead, the spell is lifted, the stone figures come back to life. A solo horn plays a simple, folk-like melody very softly. The melody passes through the orchestra, grows louder and louder, and finally blazes out in the brass in a broad, uneven rhythm, ending in a long, radiant chord.

mainIdeas.name: The celebration tune
mainIdeas.description: a short, simple melody, first on the horn, then built up through the whole orchestra.

mainIdeas.name: The final transformation
mainIdeas.description: the same tune in long, uneven beats in the brass, over ringing chords.

stops.hear: A solo horn plays a simple, gentle melody over quiet, shimmering strings
The tune passes to the strings and woodwinds, each time a little fuller
stops.happening: Kashchei’s prisoners come back to life

stops.hear: The whole orchestra plays the tune, loud and bright
The brass hammer the tune in long, uneven beats

stops.label: Last 20 seconds
stops.hear: A last brilliant, sustained chord

notice: It is the same short tune from the horn’s first notes to the last bars. Only the volume, the instruments and the rhythm change.

threads.title: Two worlds in sound
threads.body: Stravinsky gives the human characters simple, folk-like melodies, and the magic world strange, sliding, chromatic sounds. You can hear which world you are in.

threads.title: The pupil’s farewell
threads.body: The rich, colourful orchestra comes from his teacher Rimsky-Korsakov, but the jagged rhythms of the Infernal Dance already point to *The Rite of Spring*.

threads.title: From darkness to light
threads.body: The suite begins with almost nothing in the low strings and ends with the whole orchestra blazing, in the same journey as the story.
